summary: Production GraphRAG could publish and cache an answer despite WEAK, REJECTED and MISSING citation verdicts; the content gate was not on the active publication path, verifier abort/errors were ignored, and ungated legacy results could cross the service boundary. A shared post-referee publication verdict now governs ScholarlyAgent, service, SSE and caches; missing gate metadata also fails closed.
resolution_criteria: Every public GraphRAG boundary withholds prose/citations/ledger and refuses cache admission on partial audit, WEAK, REJECTED, MISSING, parse error, abort, verifier exception or missing gate metadata; the post-referee prose is the audited prose; full and adversarial tests remain green.

adjudication.decision: Adopt one deterministic fail-closed publication verdict across all public answer and cache paths.
adjudication.rationale: Identifier resolution is not claim verification. A scholarly answer with any failed or unaudited citation cannot be represented as verified or reused from cache.

summary: query_traces used is_public=true by default while the SSE writer supplied no user owner, making sufficiently long research questions and answers eligible for the public community gallery without explicit consent. TraceWriter now inserts false explicitly, a corrective migration changes the default and de-publishes legacy rows, and anonymous traces cannot be claimed through the explicit share endpoint.
resolution_criteria: Every new trace is private unless an accountable explicit publication flow records consent; anonymous traces cannot be claimed; private and capability-token share paths remain distinct; backend privacy tests pass.

adjudication.decision: Fail closed: set all query traces private by default and require explicit accountable sharing/publication.
adjudication.rationale: No reliable consent marker existed for legacy is_public rows, while a separate explicit capability-token share flow already exists. Privacy takes precedence over preserving an automatically populated gallery.
